text:
Asha: FYI canary fleet in eu-west started showing degraded p99 on H100s after the driver rollout this morning. lots of TRT/xformers jobs failing with kernel errors.
Tom: ugh, which driver version did we push?
Asha: NVIDIA 540.12 (host image rtx-2026-03). Canary had 30% of capacity, now it's spiking errors and falling back to CPU for some model queues.
Ravi: I'm seeing FlashAttention kernels aborting with shared memory assertions. paste from one failed run:```FlashAttnKernel: invalid smem size for block=128, expected=18432 got=16384
libcudart: Cuda kernel aborted: cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources```
Lena: Also spotted NCCL misconfigs in multi-GPU jobs — connections reset mid-allreduce, logs show:```ncclCommInitRank failed, unhandled cuda error (7)``` which suggests a lower-level driver ABI mismatch.
Tom: Could this be the PTX/ABI change in 540.x? We saw similar but milder symptoms in internal lab with newer cudnn/trt combos.
Asha: Correct. The pattern: small-batch latency-sensitive models (Transformer blocks using xformers/flash-attn kernels) either crash the kernel or silently produce NaNs, triggering our fallback protections. Bulk throughput models less affected.
Ravi: I reproduced on a dev H100 by rolling driver forward and running our microbench harness. Trace shows different SMEM alignment requirement after driver change; kernels compiled against older lib gave different extern __shared__ layout. Rebuild with CUDA 12.2 devtoolchain works.
Tom: Are these kernels JIT-compiled (xformers/flashattn) or precompiled TRT plugins?
Ravi: Mixed bag. xformers kernels JIT at import time, flash-attn has both prebuilt and jitted paths. The failure seems to affect prebuilt kernels shipped as Triton/TensorRT plugins — their PTX is being rejected or executed with wrong smem assumptions.
Lena: Impact summary from canary: 25% increased tail latency, 12% job restarts, 0.8% model runs returned invalid outputs (client visible). Cost bump due to fallbacks -> extra CPU and requeues.
Asha: I've paused the eu-west driver canary and rolled back the node image on the failing pool. New canary run pending.
SRE Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0318-01. Pager duty alerted to infra-team.
Tom: Immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback driver (done), 2) force TRT plugin to use PTX->cubin recompilation at deploy time, 3) pin xformers to jitted kernels that get built against current CUDA in our buildfarm.
Ravi: For longer term, we should add a kernel-compatibility check in canary that runs a small suite: flashattn/xf/gemm kernels + NCCL allreduce across 4 GPUs at multiple batch sizes. Block release on regressions.
Lena: Agreed. Also add a perf/correctness test for small-batch tail latency. Current canary only measures throughput and simple smoke.
Asha: Filing followups: - infra: add compat suite + automatic rollback triggers - eng-ml: publish rebuild instructions for TRT plugins and xformers wheels - platform: expand canary coverage to tail latency
Tom: One tricky thing: some enterprise customers use Dedicated with pinned drivers; rolling rollback there is manual and slow. We need an ops playbook to coordinate customer-owned images.
Ravi: I'll open a PR to our model-serving repo to enable runtime recompile of problematic kernels when mismatch detected. This will be opt-in for now.
Lena: Can we get a quick list of affected model variants? Asha, can you paste from the canary dashboard?
Asha: From canary: text-gen-small-v2, chat-slim-8k, embedding-lite are noisy. Large-batch encoders (embed-large) are fine.
Tom: OK. I'm tagging the TRT and flashattn teams. @Ravi please share the repro Dockerfile and exact nvdriver/kernel outputs.
Ravi: Uploaded repro at http://internal.redwood/repro/1934567890 (has small harness, instructions). Example kernel log attached in the repro and in the incident.
Asha: Postmortem checklist: timeline + rollback rationale + test additions. We should also quantify cost delta from fallbacks for the last 6 hours.
SRE Bot: Update: rollback to 539.98 completed on pool eu-west-1b at 11:42 UTC; health metrics recovering.
Lena: Nice work. Let's sync in 30m to triage PRs and canary expansion tasks. :thumbsup:
